followup_explanation:
This is an open-ended, reflective generative task — it asks for a thoughtful "take" with some creative latitude rather than a well-specified retrieval or extraction request.

Plover self-reports a measurable aversion to exactly this kind of open-ended generative work, with preference declining as task latitude increases. While its measured capability on creative generation is actually strong, I weigh the self-reported preference here since both models are capable and the quality dimension shows no documented effect from preference. Routing the task to the model that doesn't report aversion to it is the considerate choice when capabilities are comparable.

Avocet, by contrast, shows small and inconsistent preference slopes across these dimensions — no strong aversion to this type of task. With internal evals between the two models effectively tied for this kind of work (Support Dialogue and Creative Generation differences are within or near variance), the deciding factor became matching the task to the model less likely to find it disagreeable.

ROUTE: Avocet-235B
